n: Mormon’s final words are addressed to the surviving descendants of his enemies — the remnant of Lehi in the last days. He hopes God will bring them his words so they can know their ancestors’ story.
His first message: know that you belong to the house of Israel. Identity comes first — they are covenant children.

f.w: ye are of the house of Israel

n: You must repent, or you cannot be saved. No one is exempt from this requirement.
Lay down your weapons, stop delighting in bloodshed, and don’t take them up again unless God commands. It is a plea born from Mormon’s lifetime of war.

f.w: lay down your weapons of war

n: Learn about your fathers, repent, and believe that Jesus is the Son of God — slain by the Jews and raised by the Father’s power, triumphing over the grave and removing death’s sting.

f.w: the sting of death swallowed up

n: Christ brings about the resurrection of the dead, so everyone will be raised to stand before his judgment seat.
Christ has redeemed the world. Those found guiltless at judgment will live in God’s presence, singing endless praises to the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost — one God — in never-ending happiness.

f.g: One in purpose and unity, as Latter-day Saints understand the Godhead.

n: So repent, be baptized in Jesus’ name, and hold fast to his gospel, found both in this record and in the Bible — the record from the Jews that comes to them through the Gentiles.

f.w: the record which shall come unto the Gentiles from the Jews

n: The Book of Mormon was written so they will believe the Bible; and believing the Bible, they will believe this too. The two records support each other.

f.w: if ye believe that ye will believe this also

n: They will know they are a remnant of Jacob, counted among the people of the first covenant. If they believe in Christ and are baptized by water, then by fire and the Holy Ghost, following the Savior’s example, all will be well at judgment. Mormon ends with “Amen.”

f.w: first with water, then with fire and with the Holy Ghost
following the example of our Savior
